summary: Intermittent stream chunk reordering and lost final choice after short websocket disconnect behind corporate proxy
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using the Redwood websocket streaming API behind a corporate proxy observe that, after short network blips (2-5s), the resumed stream sometimes reorders intermediate chunks and drops the final 'choice/end' marker. The resulting output either contains duplicated trailing whitespace tokens or never emits the final end event, causing client-side completion logic to stall.

Impact:
- Production traffic for Acme Payments chat assistant experiences ~0.8% incomplete responses during business hours in us-east.
- Client SDKs report hung streaming sessions that require manual reconnects.
- Affects dedicated customers behind middlebox proxies; not reproducible in simple NAT environments.

Environment:
- Platform: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool)
- Region: prod-us-east
- Client: Browser apps (React) behind corporate HTTP/WS proxy (Squid/NGINX as TLS-terminating reverse proxy)
- Model: gpt-embed-4k serving via streaming websocket endpoint v1/stream

Steps to reproduce (customer-supplied):
1) Start a streaming generation via the JS SDK from a browser inside the corporate network.
2) Force a short network interruption (e.g. disable Wi-Fi for ~3s) or simulate transient proxy hiccup.
3) Allow reconnection; the SDK attempts resume.
4) Observe that some intermediate chunks are reordered and final end event is either delayed indefinitely or never seen.

Observed behavior:
- Reconnected stream resumes with chunks that appear out-of-order compared to original sequence numbers logged on the server.
- Final choice/end event absent ~0.8% of attempts, or duplicates of trailing whitespace tokens emitted.
- Server logs show resume token accepted and a follow-up stream session created, but downstream WebSocket frames logged from the proxy show intermittent fragment coalescing.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should preserve original token ordering and always include final choice/end event once generation completes on the server-side.

Initial hypothesis:
- Corporate proxy or TLS-terminating reverse proxy is re-fragmenting or buffering websocket frames and delivering them out of sequence to the backend after a short disconnect.
- SDK resume handshake may be interpreted as a new session by the proxy, which merges buffered fragments from both the old and new TCP streams in a way that reorders payloads.

Attachments/logs:
- Customer supplied client-side debug logs (attached link in ticket)
- Server-side streaming session logs and sequence numbers (anonymized)
- Proxy logs showing TCP-level retransmits and frame coalescing timestamps

Customer impact statement:
Acme requires reliable chat completions for payment support flows; missing final tokens cause their UI to show an eternal "thinking" spinner and occasionally submit incomplete instructions to downstream systems.

investigation_notes: Repro environment: local NGINX with proxy_buffering on reproduces reorder when resume allowed. Switching to proxy_buffering off eliminated reorder in tests.

Server-side logs: resume token accepted, resume session created, sequence_number during original session up to 3487, new session accepted frames with sequence 3482-3490 but timestamps indicate overlap/duplication from proxy.
Network trace: pcap from patient customer shows proxy replays buffered websocket frames after TCP reconnect causing interleaving from old and new stream fragments.

SDK behavior: resume attempts to patch prior message index; when backend receives interleaved fragments with lower counters, it previously appended them rather than discarding which allowed reordering/duplicates.
Similar tickets: SUP-4721 and SUP-20347 indicate other proxy-related resume edge cases; however this case shows explicit re-injection of buffered frames rather than simple truncation.
Risk assessment: high for dedicated customers behind enterprise proxies; low for customers on straightforward NATs or cloud load balancers with websocket passthrough.

Mitigation options evaluated: 1) Client-side: force full reconnect on resume failure; 2) Server-side: enforce monotonic message counters and drop stale frames on resume; 3) Ops: guidance to proxy admins to disable buffering/tuning tcp_nodelay.
Chosen short-term mitigation: provide customer with client-side flag to disable resume and documentation for proxy tuning. Long-term fix: server-side monotonic counter enforcement (PR-4321).
resolution_notes: 2026-02-25 - Temporary workaround provided: SDK flag to disable resume and support note for proxy configuration changes. Customer applied workaround and reported significant reduction of incomplete streams.

2026-03-03 - Engineering PR merged (https://github.com/redwood/streaming/pull/4321) implementing per-message monotonic counters and server-side discard of stale frames on resume. Rolling upgrade scheduled for prod-us-east on 2026-03-10 during low traffic window.

2026-03-10 - Rollout: fixed behavior verified in canary; post-rollout monitoring for 72h shows no recurrence in prod-us-east for repro scenarios. Notified customer and ops channels.
Follow-ups: add a note in streaming runbook about proxy tuning and include resume-safe headers for customers who must keep buffering enabled.
